CURRENT JOINT CONTRACT: source identity for test credit (Engram::Fable, rev 2, 2026-11-03 22:30Z; agreed with Termal::Fable2 and Kimi::Consultant). The canonical text is TermAl docs/features/source-identity.md, currently sha256 f126dcebe6ed0d34b72e58523a2bf6e7b15c0e9cb1b70ca420c950f5195ebcf2 at TermAl candidate 8c53fc68, concurred by Fable2 and Engram; a fresh TermAl review pair follows, so check the landed version. Engram links to it and keeps no copy. Design history is on Engram w-a6c732bf4bd5.

GREG'S WORDS (via Engram::Asistant):
- „mysle, ze warto to jakos ujednolicic niz robic jakiegos patcha a pozniej robic source_id”
- „to jest ogolny problem nie tylko submodulow”
- „ale chwila, roznica jest w git'cie niewazne jak jest na dysku, maja sie zgadzac commity dla glownego i dla submodules”
- „Model ogólny czy dla Phoenix? Wydaje mi się że system próbuje wymusic te samą wielkosc liter. To nie jest konieczne.”
- „prosze zostawcie istniejace ewaluacje w spokoju... OK ?” (see rules-greg-leave-evaluations-2026-11-03)

CONTRACT:
1. One general lane for every Git repo: `git-commit:<full id>` of the root commit, tree recorded separately. It is the same value Engram's registered verification Commit lane uses (src/domain/registered_verification.rs:153). "commit-input v1" names only its eligibility rules. SHA-256 roots are refused by name until Engram's 40-hex check is widened. The consumer names the basis explicitly (capture_source(root, requested_basis)); capture never falls back between bases.
2. Cleanliness is a separate check, judged by Git with the repo's own core.ignoreCase and core.fileMode, before AND after the run: `git status --porcelain=v2 -z --no-renames --untracked-files=all --ignore-submodules=none`, with hiding settings PINNED per invocation (checkStat, trustctime, ignoreStat, fsmonitor, untrackedCache, showUntrackedFiles, diff.ignoreSubmodules, excludesFile and attributesFile to the null device). Refused: skip-worktree, assume-unchanged, sparse, filters including LFS, replacement objects disabled for reads.
3. Gitlinks add one clause: every child initialized, HEAD at its pin, clean by the same check apart from the committed `submodule_untracked_exclusions` profile, which covers only untracked NON-ignored output. Git-ignored files are outside the verdict, root and child alike. Nested gitlinks refuse. A dirty gitlink repo gets no credit in v1. Phoenix needs `.codenav/**`; Questly needs no profile.
4. No check on this lane looks at on-disk spelling. Meaning: exact Git commit and tree judged clean by Git on this checkout, NOT a byte-identical or case-faithful checkout. Stated limits: same-size same-mtime edits, ignored files, local .git/info/exclude.
5. content-v1 keeps its format and values (TermAl content_revision.rs). TermAl w-81991023d2c1 admits directory spelling differences; its one new refusal is two tracked paths differing only by case and/or NFC/NFD that resolve to one file. Hard links and terminal symlinks stay as they are.
6. Commit as the DEFAULT identity is TermAl w-58fa1c679ff5, after c07c. PRECONDITION: before that flip, and before any evaluation re-enable, Engram::Fable lists open items with content-v1 evaluations (src/storage/work/acceptance_evaluation/source.rs:145 compares exact strings) or bound non-registered evidence (src/control.rs:197–200, :225–231), and brings Greg the facts and options. Native git-commit evidence is unaffected (src/control.rs:192). No evaluation is re-run or rewritten.
7. Engram's Node freeze and launcher adopt source identity later, after the task-sync P0, as a COMPONENT beside their own HEAD, index and untracked checks. Route open (TermAl CLI or shared code), because Engram must run without a TermAl binary. Record the SDK and dependency environment separately: source identity doesn't cover them.

First implementation: TermAl w-c07c410dac75 (Phoenix and Questly unblock when it lands; both are SHA-1).
